vulns.summary: pypdf: Possible infinite loop when hitting EOF in standard xref table
vulns.details:
### Impact

An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to an infinite loop. This requires an incomplete file which ends inside the xref table.

### Patches

This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.20.0](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.20.0).

### Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4170](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4170).

### Notes

This has been reported through both the secure channel and as a public issue at [#4169](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/issues/4169).

vulns.summary: pypdf: Unvalidated JPEG image data loading
vulns.details:
### Impact

An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to arbitrary image parsers being called. This requires loading an image which claims to use the `/DCTDecode` filter (JPEG data).

Users which do not have the optional *Pillow* dependency installed in their environment are not affected.

### Patches

This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.1](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.1).

### Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4222](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4222).

vulns.summary: pypdf has possible long runtimes/large memory usage for encrypted PDF files
vulns.details:
### Impact

An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to large runtimes/memory usage. This requires accessing the page count of an encrypted PDF file, which itself declares a wrong `/Count` value.

### Patches

This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.3](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.3).

### Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4270](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4270).

### Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4240](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4240).

vulns.summary: pypdf: Possible long runtimes for repeated malformed cross-reference entries (Follow-up)
vulns.details:
### Impact

An attacker who uses this vulnerability can craft a PDF which leads to long runtimes. This requires cross-reference streams with repeated malformed cross-reference streams.

### Patches

This has been fixed in [pypdf==6.21.2](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/releases/tag/6.21.2).

### Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade yet, consider applying the changes from PR [#4240](https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/pull/4240).

### Notes

This is a follow-up to https://github.com/py-pdf/pypdf/security/advisories/GHSA-55h5-xmcq-c37v, which had the side-effect of still loading the whole stream again despite the cache being present.
